answer: Personal finance starts with understanding income, tracking expenses, planning a budget, and saving toward clear goals.
Income is money received; expenses are money spent. A sustainable plan keeps expenses within income.
Choose a target and date, subtract what you already have, then divide the remainder into manageable monthly contributions.
The 50/30/20 guide assigns 50% to needs, 30% to wants, and 20% to savings. Adjust it to your situation.
Common mistakes include spending before planning, ignoring small purchases, and waiting to save whatever is left.
Helpful student habits include checking balances, recording purchases, comparing prices, and saving a small amount regularly.
Start with a small amount you can repeat. A common guide is 20% of income, adjusted for your essentials.
List your income, cover needs first, choose limits for wants, and reserve money for savings.
A need supports basic living, study, or safety. A want improves comfort but can usually wait.
Pay at least the minimum on every debt, then direct extra money to one balance at a time.
